features.t: VPCs (create, describe, delete, DNS attribute settings)
x: Secondary IPv4 CIDR blocks (and an Amazon-provided IPv6 block) can be associated/disassociated with EC2 validation (/16-/28, private ranges, no overlap, max 5, blocked while subnets exist); local routes and netsim follow. IPAM pools/allocations are not simulated.

features.t: Subnets (create, describe, delete)
x: Private IPv4s are allocated from the subnet CIDR like EC2 (.0-.3 and the broadcast address reserved); public IPv4 only with MapPublicIpOnLaunch / AssociatePublicIpAddress / an EIP.

features.t: Route tables (create, describe, delete, routes, subnet associations, main table)
x: Behaviour comes from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim): routes (longest prefix), IGW/NAT/peering semantics, the SG union and stateless NACLs incl. the ephemeral return path decide every Reachability Analyzer answer — on Nano that evaluated behaviour is the network (in-browser instances exchange no packets).

features.t: Internet gateways (create, attach, detach, delete)
x: Behaviour comes from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim): routes (longest prefix), IGW/NAT/peering semantics, the SG union and stateless NACLs incl. the ephemeral return path decide every Reachability Analyzer answer — on Nano that evaluated behaviour is the network (in-browser instances exchange no packets).

features.t: NAT gateways (create, describe, delete)
x: Evaluated like AWS: the route works only while the NAT gateway exists, is public and sits in a subnet that routes to an attached internet gateway, and that subnet's NACL applies in both directions. Offline with enforcement on, egress is really translated (masquerade) — but the internet sees the appliance host's address, not the NAT gateway's EIP, and the NAT keeps the client's source port (real NAT GW uses 1024-65535).

features.t: Network ACLs (create, describe, delete, numbered allow/deny entries, subnet associations)
x: Behaviour comes from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim): routes (longest prefix), IGW/NAT/peering semantics, the SG union and stateless NACLs incl. the ephemeral return path decide every Reachability Analyzer answer — on Nano that evaluated behaviour is the network (in-browser instances exchange no packets).

features.t: Security groups (create, authorize/revoke rules, delete, default-SG protection)
x: Behaviour comes from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim): routes (longest prefix), IGW/NAT/peering semantics, the SG union and stateless NACLs incl. the ephemeral return path decide every Reachability Analyzer answer — on Nano that evaluated behaviour is the network (in-browser instances exchange no packets).

features.t: Elastic IPs (allocate, associate, disassociate, release)
x: Allocated addresses are synthetic (not real internet-routable IPs).

features.t: Egress-only internet gateways (create, describe, delete)
DHCP option sets (create, describe, delete, associate)
x: Enforced, not stored config: DescribeVpcDnsResolution computes the VPC's effective DNS server(s) live from its DHCP option set + enableDnsSupport attribute (AmazonProvidedDNS → the VPC's reserved resolver address; a custom domain-name-servers value → those real IPs) — changing either really changes the answer, and whether a subnet can actually reach a custom resolver is a normal Reachability Analyzer check (route table + SG/NACL).

features.t: Managed prefix lists (create, describe, delete)
VPC peering connections (create, accept, describe, delete)
x: The analyzer routes across an ACTIVE peering (non-transitive; the peer's route table needs the return route). Offline packet enforcement across peered VPCs is compiled but not yet covered by the real-packet test, and VPCs with overlapping CIDRs cannot be enforced on one Docker host.

features.t: VPC Route Server (create, describe, delete)
x: Only the resource lifecycle is modeled — no real BGP peering or route exchange.

features.t: VPC/subnet Flow logs
x: CreateFlowLogs / DescribeFlowLogs / DeleteFlowLogs manage real flow log resources (status, destination, format, tags) against a VPC, subnet or ENI.

features.t: VPC Integrations tab: transit gateway attachments and Network Manager registration
x: Shows this VPC's real transit gateway attachments and whether each gateway is registered in a Network Manager global network (core/networkmanager_core.py, Home Region us-west-2). Third-party partner integrations (Aviatrix, Kentik and similar) are external services and are not simulated.

features.t: AWS Network Manager global networks, sites, devices, links and transit gateway registrations
x: Inventory and registration control plane only: transit gateways are validated against the account's real EC2 model. No topology telemetry, events, route analysis, Connect or Direct Connect associations are collected.

features.t: "VPC and more" wizard (auto-generated subnets/route tables/NAT gateways/endpoints)
x: Pure orchestration over primitives that are each already full (CreateVpc/CreateSubnet/CreateRouteTable/CreateInternetGateway/CreateNatGateway/CreateVpcEndpoint) — Name tag auto-generation, AZ/public/private subnet counts, NAT gateways ($) and the S3 Gateway VPC endpoint option all run real calls in sequence. IPAM-allocated CIDRs and the VPC encryption control ($) field are not modeled (same gaps as plain CreateVpc).

features.t: Subnet CIDR reservations
Subnet sharing (AWS RAM)
x: core/ram_core.py models the real RAM object: resource shares, resource/principal associations and their state machine, with real validation (only subnet/security-group ARNs, must exist) and real owner-side enforcement (a shared subnet cannot be deleted while an association is ASSOCIATED — vpc_core._delete_subnet checks ram_store).

features.t: Route table edge associations (internet gateway / virtual private gateway)
x: IGW and VGW edge associations are stored with AWS validation (the gateway must be attached to the table's VPC, one table per gateway). Gateway route tables (ingress routing) are not evaluated by netsim; Outposts / Local Gateway edge associations need physical hardware and are not simulated.

features.t: Route table route propagation (Virtual Private Gateway)
x: EnableVgwRoutePropagation copies the VGW's static VPN prefixes into the route table as propagated routes (origin EnableVgwRoutePropagation, listed in the Routes tab, updated on VPN route/attach/detach changes) and netsim honours them. BGP-learned prefixes need a real peer and are never propagated.

features.t: Network Access Analyzer (scopes, findings)
x: Reuses the same netsim evaluator as Reachability Analyzer: an access scope's match paths name source/destination resource ids (empty = every ENI / the internet); StartNetworkInsightsAccessScopeAnalysis runs reach() over every resolved pair with protocol=tcp, port=None — "is there an UNRESTRICTED path" (the question the real built-in "internet-accessible resources" scope answers) — and records a finding per reachable pair.

features.t: Security group sharing (AWS RAM), VPC associations, related resources
x: Same real RAM object model as aws.vpc.resource-sharing, scoped to security-group ARNs: a shared SG cannot be deleted while an association is ASSOCIATED (vpc_core._delete_security_group checks ram_store). "Related resources" lists real ENIs/instances using the group; "VPC associations" shows the owning VPC.

features.t: NAT gateway CloudWatch monitoring
x: AWS/NATGateway metrics (ActiveConnectionCount, ConnectionEstablishedCount, BytesOutToDestination, PacketsOutToDestination) are real CloudWatch datapoints pushed by vpc_core._push_nat_metrics every time the shared reachability evaluator actually traverses this NAT gateway with a passing verdict (AnalyzeReachability / Reachability Analyzer / Network Access Analyzer) — never synthetic background data.

features.t: VPC console preferences
x: VPC Block Public Access is real and enforced: ModifyVpcBlockPublicAccessOptions changes netsim's internet_egress()/_reach_from_external() decisions directly (block-bidirectional blocks IGW egress AND ingress, block-ingress blocks only inbound), honored by Reachability Analyzer and the offline packet enforcer alike; exclusions (CreateVpcBlockPublicAccessExclusion) really exempt a VPC/subnet.

features.t: PrivateLink (VPC endpoints, endpoint services)
x: Gateway endpoints (S3/DynamoDB) are real: CreateVpcEndpoint adds a route (dest = the service's address ranges, target = the vpce- id) to every chosen route table, and core/netsim's GATEWAY_ENDPOINT route kind makes Reachability Analyzer and the offline packet enforcer both honor it as a live hop.

features.t: VPC Lattice control plane (service networks, services, listeners/rules, target groups, associations, resource gateways/configurations, domain verifications, auth policies)
x: Control plane is real (core/vpc_lattice_core, native vpc-lattice REST): AWS name/ID/ARN formats, VPC/subnet/security-group/instance checks against the EC2 model, one service network per VPC, unique listener ports and rule priorities, undeletable default rule, in-use target groups/gateways/networks refuse deletion, auth/resource policy and tag APIs.

features.t: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall (rule groups, rules, domain lists, VPC associations)
x: Control plane is real with Route 53 Resolver validation: domain syntax (wildcards only as a leading *.), ADD/REMOVE/REPLACE semantics, rule priorities, BLOCK needs BlockResponse (OVERRIDE needs a CNAME domain), association priority 100-9900 unique per VPC, existing-VPC and in-use ConflictException checks. The Resolver decision is evaluated on both substrates through the simulator verb Route53Resolver.ResolveDnsQuery (VpcId, DomainName, QueryType): VPC associations then rules by priority, exact + leading-wildcard domains, ALLOW/ALERT/BLOCK with NODATA/NXDOMAIN/OVERRIDE (CNAME) answers. There is no live Route 53 Resolver: no real DNS query from an instance is filtered and no query logs are produced.

features.t: AWS Network Firewall (firewalls, policies, stateless/stateful/Suricata/domain rule groups, TLS inspection, resource policies, logging, endpoint associations)
x: Control plane is real with AWS validation: subnet/VPC mappings must exist (one subnet per AZ), protection flags, UpdateToken optimistic concurrency, typed rule-group references, rule-group capacity, Suricata rule strings (sid required/unique), stateless priorities/match attributes, domain lists, resource policy JSON, logging destinations. The rule evaluator (stateless priority order + default actions, then stateful 5-tuple/Suricata/domain allow-deny) is wired into the shared netsim path on both substrates: a route whose target is a firewall endpoint (vpce- from DescribeFirewall / VPC endpoint associations) makes AnalyzeReachability and Network Insights run the packet through the firewall policy (NETWORK_FIREWALL_DROP names the rule), then forward via the firewall subnet's route table; NetworkFirewall.SimulateTraffic evaluates one packet (incl. HttpHost/TlsSni) directly. Not modelled: packet-level enforcement offline (such routes are enforced as drop with a warning), the return path through the endpoint, domain/SNI rules in AnalyzeReachability (no L7 context in a reachability query), alert/flow/TLS log delivery, TLS decryption. Container associations are not simulated.

features.t: Site-to-Site VPN and Client VPN (customer/virtual private gateways, VPN connections, VPN concentrators, Client VPN endpoints)
x: Control plane is real: customer gateways, virtual private gateways (attach/detach), VPN connections with generated tunnel options/PSKs, static routes and tunnel option edits, VPN concentrators, Client VPN endpoints with target networks, authorization rules and routes, all with AWS validation and dependency checks. VGW-propagated and static VPN prefixes are followed by the route tables and honoured by the netsim/Reachability Analyzer.

features.t: AWS Verified Access (instances, trust providers, groups, endpoints)
x: Instances/trust providers/groups/endpoints are real objects over the native EC2 API (the same protocol real Verified Access uses), and VerifyAccessEndpointPolicy really evaluates the endpoint's/group's policy document against user-supplied context — the same thing the AWS console's own "Test policy" tool does, so policy logic is genuinely exercised.

features.t: Transit Gateway (gateways, VPC attachments, route tables, static/propagated routes, associations, propagations)
x: VPC attachments only; peering, VPN, Connect and Direct Connect attachments are not modelled. Forwarding between attached VPCs is evaluated by the Reachability Analyzer and enforced by the netsim rules (route-table association, longest-prefix match, propagation, return routes in both the TGW tables and the VPC route tables), but no real packets traverse a transit gateway and no TGW flow logs or metrics are produced. Cross-account sharing and appliance-mode flow stickiness are stored, not enforced.

features.t: Transit Gateway policy tables, multicast domains, metering policies
x: Policy tables, multicast domains (subnet associations, static group members/sources, group search) and metering policies (+ entries) are real control-plane state with validation. Policy tables and metering rules are stored, not evaluated against traffic; there is no multicast data plane. Transit Gateway peering, Connect and VPN attachments are not modelled.

features.t: Traffic Mirroring (mirror sessions, targets, filters)
x: Targets, filters with ordered accept/reject rules and sessions are real control-plane state with AWS validation (rule numbers, protocol/port rules, session number per source ENI, in-use checks) and the filter rules can be evaluated against a packet. No packets are VXLAN-encapsulated to the target ENI / NLB: nothing listening on a mirror target sees traffic. Offline with netsim enforcement on (VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1|auto, Docker compute backend) the enforcer's real per-flow counters ARE evaluated against the sessions (lowest session number claims a packet; filter rules decide accept/reject; PacketLength truncates bytes) and each window's mirrored FLOW SUMMARIES are written to CloudWatch Logs group /vyomi/traffic-mirror/<session-id> (stream = source ENI). Nano has no data plane, so no flows exist there.

features.t: Reachability Analyzer (Network Insights paths + analyses, AnalyzeReachability)
x: Answers come from the shared netsim evaluator (the same one the offline enforcer compiles to nftables and the real-packet test checks). Explanation codes map to the closest native code (ENI_SG_RULES_MISMATCH, SUBNET_ACL_RESTRICTION, NO_ROUTE_TO_DESTINATION); other blocks report the netsim code. Transit gateways, VPN, endpoints and load balancers are not path components.

features.t: Network Firewall container associations
x: Container associations attach Network Firewall to container platforms (EKS/ECS) through firewall endpoints on real node networking; Vyomi has no inline firewall data path for them.

features.t: Create several subnets in one console submit (a CreateSubnet call per subnet over the native wire)
x: The console loops one CreateSubnet call per row, like the real console; there is no batch API, and a failure part-way leaves the earlier subnets created (reported in the message).

features.t: All VPC resources summary (live counts per Region)
x: Vyomi simulates one Region (us-east-1); the page lists live counts for it and states that other Regions are not modeled — no cross-Region data exists to aggregate.

features.t: VPC encryption control
x: VPC Encryption Controls: Create / Describe / Modify / DeleteVpcEncryptionControl and GetVpcResourcesBlockingEncryptionEnforcement (one control per VPC, monitor and enforce modes, resource exclusions, creating -> available). The audit runs over the VPC's real resources and enforcement is real: switching to enforce is refused while non-excluded unencrypted resources exist, and in an enforced VPC RunInstances of an instance type that cannot encrypt traffic is rejected.
